title: Smooth four-dimensional Poincaré formulation and bounded reconnaissance
formulation: For every smooth, closed 4-manifold X that is homotopy equivalent to the standard 4-sphere S^4, determine whether X is diffeomorphic to S^4. This dossier uses orientation-preserving diffeomorphism after choosing orientations; any orientation convention used by a subgoal must be stated separately.
scope: The flagship is restricted to the smooth category, closed manifolds, and the homotopy-sphere hypothesis. It prepares source material and bounded evidence tasks; it does not treat a candidate as a resolution merely because it is difficult to distinguish from S^4.
out_of_scope: Topological classification, PL classification, arbitrary homology 4-spheres, smooth Schoenflies, and claims about every Gluck twist are distinct topics unless a future ledger object states an implication and receives independent review.
motivation: Dimension four is where topological and smooth classification pull apart most sharply. A careful flagship can make those category boundaries visible while giving agents bounded, falsifiable work instead of an invitation to announce a famous-problem solution.
falsifier: A counterexample to the smooth formulation would be a smooth closed homotopy 4-sphere accompanied by independently checked evidence that it is not diffeomorphic to standard S^4. A claimed proof is falsified by a failed inference, a mismatched hypothesis, or an invariant/certificate that does not establish its stated conclusion.
settlement_conditions: No resolution-shaped disposition may be requested from this dossier. Any future result claim must enter under-result-review with a complete statement-to-artifact correspondence, independent reviews by qualified external experts, and a specific account of the category and equivalence relation used.
no_resolution_language: This is a draft source dossier, not a solution announcement. It makes no claim that the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré question has been resolved, and no share text may imply that it has.
safety: Mathematical source preparation only. Do not present unreviewed diagrams, computations, or model output as expert certification; do not upload private correspondence or hidden reasoning.
external_expert_requirements: Before publication, obtain independent written review from at least two external smooth-4-manifold specialists, with one specifically checking category distinctions and one checking each cited anchor. Any claimed theorem-level advance also requires a reviewer with direct expertise in the technique used (for example, handles, gauge theory, or trisections).

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: A qualified external reviewer must recheck the formulation, literature anchors, and any purported resolution status immediately before the source enters the real sharpening workflow.

variant_distinctions.distinction: The smooth formulation asks for a diffeomorphism. A topological homeomorphism theorem is not a diffeomorphism theorem and cannot be used here as a smooth resolution.

The PL formulation is retained as a separately named category question. This dossier neither identifies PL equivalence with smooth diffeomorphism nor infers one category's conclusion from another without a reviewed theorem.
A homology 4-sphere is not automatically within this formulation. The flagship requires an explicit homotopy-equivalence hypothesis before a candidate is treated as relevant.
A Gluck-twist calculation is a bounded construction question. It is not evidence that all Gluck twists are standard or that the smooth Poincaré formulation follows.

bounded_subgoals.question: For one named 2-knot and one fully supplied Kirby or trisection description, check whether the proposed Gluck-twist handle moves produce the stated manifold.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: A move fails, a framing convention is inconsistent, or an independently recomputed invariant disagrees with the claimed target.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One supplied candidate and one declared convention set only; this task makes no universal claim about Gluck twists or exotic S^4.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: A versioned diagram inventory, explicit move ledger, and two independently generated invariant calculations.

bounded_subgoals.question: For a finite, supplied trisection diagram, compute the explicitly named diagrammatic invariant and test its stated behavior under one listed stabilization move.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: The parser rejects the diagram, the stabilization test changes a purported invariant, or an independent recomputation disagrees.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: The task is a finite diagram check and does not assert that the invariant classifies smooth homotopy 4-spheres.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Machine-readable diagram input, deterministic computation log, stabilization fixture, and a reviewer rerun record.

bounded_subgoals.question: Build a citation-to-claim map for one named candidate construction, distinguishing topological, smooth, and PL conclusions at every edge.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: Any map edge lacks a primary anchor, changes category without a cited theorem, or attributes a stronger conclusion than its source states.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: Literature mapping only; it neither validates the candidate nor resolves the flagship.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Anchored citation table with page or theorem locators and independent category-audit notes.
